claims.text: The route deviation is established on the governing measurement. The trace runs 23.97 km against a booked optimal of 18.0 km — an excess of 5.97 km, or 33.17% — so both POL-RD-01 gates are passed: 33.17% is above the 20% percentage threshold and 5.97 km is above the 0.8 km absolute threshold. The threshold test is run on gps_trace.trace_distance_km, as POL-RD-01 requires; the 24.0 km figure on the trip record is the rounded convenience copy and is not the figure the test is run on.

The trace carrying that measurement is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 241 fixes at a 10.0 second sample interval, 100% coverage, no gaps at all and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. None of limbs (a) to (c) is met — no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m, no sustained interval above 30 seconds — so the deviation rests on a clean trace and needs no corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii).

The deviation is corroborated in any event by two independent sources. The payment ledger charges a gantry at PIE (Adam Rd towards Tuas) which the ledger itself flags on_optimal_route false, and the trace's nearest fix to that gantry is 8.76 m — the vehicle provably crossed a gantry the optimal route never uses. The driver separately admitted the route in the chat log — 'AYE jam boss, this way faster' — which is a driver admission placing the vehicle off the optimal corridor under POL-RD-07(ii).

No traffic-advisory exoneration is available under POL-RD-03. The only advisory artifact in this bundle, EV-ADVIS-00114-01, carries no payload at all: it is MISSING and carries weight 0.0. There is therefore no advisory naming a road or segment the optimal route traverses, no validity window to overlap the trip, and nothing against which the actual route can be matched. The absence of any advisory is itself citable, and the driver's own statement concedes 'No advisory that I know of.'

No rider-requested detour exists under POL-RD-04. The only rider message in the chat log is a complaint against the route, 'adam road?? jurong is the other way', sent at 18:58:40 — the opposite of an instruction — and its waypoint_hint is null with no road named as a request. Nothing in the chat log asks the driver to go via the PIE, the AYE or anywhere else, and the excess is therefore not attributable to any rider instruction.

No exculpatory adjustment to the baseline is available under POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12. Both pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so there is no relocation and the baseline stays at the booked 18.0 km; and the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so there is no matched pooled itinerary and no collect-and-set-down distance to exclude. The 5.97 km excess survives every adjustment the policy provides.

The driver's justification does not survive the record. His account is that he went 'up and over on the PIE' because it 'moved', but no artifact supports that a named corridor was closed or restricted, and the trip record shows the journey took 40.0 minutes against an optimal duration of 30.0 minutes. POL-RD-03 requires a specific advisory, not an untested assertion of congestion, and POL-RD-08 provides that a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden.

The rider's burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on the face of the artifacts: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry the same trip identifier TRP-00114 with consistent pickup and trip timestamps, and the excess of 5.97 km / 33.17% is measured from an unimpaired trace. Nor does the extra-corroboration condition fire: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and that single claim is substantiated (deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1), so no corroboration beyond the trace is required in any event.

With the deviation established and no clause excusing it, POL-RD-02 fixes the refund arithmetically. The fare model is METERED, so the clause runs: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 18.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.6, the surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 of on-optimal-route ERP = 44.42, against a charged_total of 58.10. The refund is 13.68, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 as SGD 13.70. That is 23.5% of charged_total, well under the 90% share that would convert the outcome to FULL_REFUND, so the ruling is PARTIAL_REFUND. The rider does not dispute the 1.6 surge and it is applied in the driver's favour in this computation.

The off-route ERP is itemised but must not be added on top. The 2.00 PIE (Adam Rd towards Tuas) charge is off the optimal route and is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 figure, because the recomputed fare counts only the 2.50 gantry lying on the optimal route. Under POL-RD-09(1) that line is shown separately for transparency and never double-counted, so the rider's recoverable sum is 13.70, not 15.70.

No standalone billing-integrity correction is available under POL-RD-09(4), and the rider does not ask for one. Both charged gantry lines are matched to the trace within the 250 m radius: the PIE (Kim Keat Link towards Tuas) gantry has a nearest fix at 0.0 m and the PIE (Adam Rd towards Tuas) gantry at 8.76 m. Neither line is phantom, so the only route to a refund on this case is the POL-RD-02 recomputation set out above.

No repeat-deviation uplift is sought and none is available. The excess here (33.17%, 5.97 km) is not a MATERIAL deviation, being below both the 50% and 8.0 km materiality gates, so the POL-RD-06 check is not triggered; and on the correct field no pattern is established in any case — driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 412, a ratio of 0.0024 against the 0.05 threshold. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags (2) is a different field and may not be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure under POL-GEN-01. The rider therefore seeks the POL-RD-02 partial of SGD 13.70, not a FULL_REFUND uplift.

Nothing in POL-RD-10 requires escalation and the case should be decided on the money. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, so limb (2) is not met; the timestamps do not conflict by more than 10 minutes, so limb (4) is not met; the trace is unimpaired under limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07, so limb (3) is not met; the refund of 13.70 is far below SGD 150.00 and below charged_total, so limb (6) is not met; and every charge line has a counterpart in the trace, so limb (8) is not met. A holding escalation would leave the rider's money with the platform, which is not the outcome this record supports.

claims.text: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement, and that field reads 23.97 km, not the rounded 24.0 km carried on the trip record; the excess is therefore 5.97 km, and the rider's 'extra 6 km' overstates the figure that the clause actually measures. The trace is complete (100% coverage, 241 fixes, zero gaps, 10 s sampling), so no rival figure can displace it.

On the governing trace the excess is 5.97 km and 33.17% of the 18.0 km optimal. That clears the establishment gates (0.8 km / 20%) but falls short of the materiality gates (8.0 km absolute / 50%), so this is an ESTABLISHED BUT NOT MATERIAL deviation. POL-RD-06 is not engaged: no driver_profile pattern uplift to FULL_REFUND and no driver-conduct referral can follow from this trip.

Even if POL-RD-06 were consulted, no pattern is established, and the rider must not be allowed to build one from the wrong counter: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 412, a ratio of roughly 0.0024, far below the 0.05-with-40-trips test. prior_deviation_flags (2) is a LIFETIME counter and POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting it for the trailing-90-day field the clause names.

Under POL-RD-02 the refund is arithmetic, not discretionary, and it is capped there: charged_total 58.10 less recomputed_fare 44.42 leaves 13.68, rounded UP to SGD 13.70. That is less than the 15.00 the rider contests, and it is the ceiling on this claim — the rider is entitled to the computed figure and nothing more.

The recomputation preserves the driver's lawful-route earnings intact: the 1.6x multiplier the rider expressly accepts is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and applied to the optimal distance and time, so base, distance, time and surge on the 18.0 km route all stand. Only the excess-distance component moves; the surge is untouched and is not refundable.

The rider's '$4.50 of ERP' claim adds nothing. The PIE (Kim Keat Link towards Tuas) gantry at $2.50 lies ON the optimal route and is credited inside the recomputed fare; the PIE (Adam Rd towards Tuas) gantry at $2.00 is the only off-optimal line and is ALREADY comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund, which under POL-RD-09(1) must never be added on top. Nor is the Adam Rd line a phantom charge attracting a separate POL-RD-09(4) correction: the trace's nearest fix is 8.76 m from that gantry, well inside the 250 m match radius, so the vehicle demonstrably crossed it and the line is matched.

The one exculpatory route open to the driver cannot be run on this record: POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory, and the only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-00114-01, is MISSING, carrying no payload and weight 0.0. The driver's account that the AYE was crawling from the Alexandra exit therefore cannot be tested, and under POL-RD-10(5) an exculpatory clause invoked against an artifact that can carry no fact is a terminal ESCALATE — the disputed amount is held rather than refunded, which is the correct disposition of a record that cannot answer the question either way.

The remaining exculpatory clauses are equally unavailable and the record should not be stretched to pretend otherwise: POL-RD-04 fails because the chat log carries the rider's complaint ('adam road?? jurong is the other way'), not a rider instruction, and waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so the corroboration test is undecidable and the clause cannot run; POL-RD-05 fails because pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null; POL-RD-12 fails because vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this case cannot be finally decided on the present record, so it is escalated to a human reviewer and the SGD 15.00 in dispute is held — neither collected nor refunded — pending that review.

What is agreed, and what would otherwise decide the money. The deviation is established on the governing measurement: the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00114) runs 23.97 km against the 18.0 km booked optimal (EV-TRIP-00114), an excess of 5.97 km / 33.17%. That clears the POL-RD-01 gates (0.8 km and 20%) but is below the materiality gates (8.0 km and 50%), so no repeat-deviation uplift and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06 arises. Had the money been ruled on, POL-RD-02 would give: charged_total SGD 58.10; recomputed_fare SGD 44.42, being (base 3.80 + 0.75 x 18.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x the 1.6 surge read from EV-FARE-00114, plus 0.80 platform fee and 2.50 of on-optimal-route ERP; refund SGD 13.68, rounded up to SGD 13.70. The SGD 2.00 PIE (Adam Rd) gantry is off the optimal route but is already comprehended in that figure and must not be added on top (POL-RD-09(1)); both charged gantry lines are matched to the trace within the 250 m radius and there is no billing-integrity correction. The rider's SGD 15.00 is capped by that arithmetic, and the 1.6 surge the rider accepts is preserved to the driver.

Why no money ruling issues. The driver met the deviation with a traffic explanation — the AYE crawling from the Alexandra exit, 'up and over on the PIE' — which is the road-closure / traffic-advisory exoneration ground in POL-RD-03. That clause reads a traffic_advisory, and the only advisory artifact for this trip, EV-ADVIS-00114-01, carries no payload and a weight_multiplier of 0.0: it can carry no fact, and its absence is itself citable (POL-GEN-02). An exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact that lacks the field the clause requires is a mandatory ground of escalation under POL-RD-10(5); the missing advisory is a failure of the record, not a finding against the driver, and neither a party's account nor a stated reason can stand in for the artifact the clause reads. POL-RD-10(5) is terminal: it replaces the ruling, so amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd are null and the SGD 15.00 is held.

What would resolve it. A TRAFFIC_ADVISORY for TRP-00114 covering 2026-08-07 18:40–19:20 SGT that names the AYE (Alexandra exit) or the PIE corridor the optimal route traverses, with its validity window and the shortest lawful alternative distance, so that POL-RD-03 can be run; failing that, a platform statement that no advisory was issued for that window, which would let the POL-RD-02 figure of SGD 13.70 be released to the rider.

Referrals. None: POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct review needs a material deviation and an established pattern (neither is present) and POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity finds no unmatched charge line. Confidence is reported at 0.4, below the platform floor of 0.70, which independently engages POL-RD-10(1). Both parties correctly declined to use the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags, which is context-only under POL-GEN-01.

To both parties. This trip deviated, and the refund is the arithmetic one.

THE DEVIATION. POL-RD-01 measures the excess on gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which is 23.97 km, against the booked optimal of 18.0 km — an excess of 5.97 km, or 33.2%. The 24.0 km on the trip record is the rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and is not the figure the threshold test uses. Both establishment gates are passed (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so the deviation is established. The excess reaches neither materiality gate (50% or 8.0 km), so this is not a MATERIAL deviation and POL-RD-06 is not engaged: there is no repeat-deviation uplift and no driver-conduct referral. The rider's profile does not change this either — deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the threshold of 4, so no corroboration beyond the trace is required. The trace is clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (241 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gap over 90 s, no jump over 500 m), so the deviation needs no corroboration; in any event the fare ledger's off-optimal Adam Road gantry independently places the vehicle off the optimal corridor, and the driver's chat message — 'AYE jam boss, this way faster' — admits the reroute.

NO EXCUSE RUNS. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction and the only rider message is a complaint about the route, not a request; waypoint_hint is null, so that test cannot be run. POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 do not apply (no endpoint was amended; the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL). POL-RD-03 requires a traffic advisory and there is none. The driver's account that the AYE was crawling is a general assertion that traffic was bad, and POL-RD-08 is explicit that such an assertion, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden. I do NOT escalate on the empty advisory (EV-ADVIS-00114-01, no payload, weight 0.0). POL-RD-10(5) fires where an exculpatory clause is invoked against a CITED artifact that is missing; here the driver cites no evidence at all and his own statement records 'No advisory that I know of.' The advisory's absence is itself citable and defeats the excuse on the merits; it is not a gap that stops the case being decided on a complete, unimpaired trace.

THE MONEY. The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 18.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.6) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 on-route ERP = 44.42. The 1.6 multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and is preserved on the optimal route — the rider accepts the surge and the recomputation charges it. charged_total is 58.10. The refund is 58.10 - 44.42 = 13.68, rounded UP to SGD 13.70. That is 23.6% of the charge, well short of the 90% that would convert it to a full refund and well above the 0.50 de minimis, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. Charged total is 58.10. Refund = 58.10 - 44.42 = 13.68, rounded up to SGD 13.70. That is 23.5% of the charge, short of the 90% share that would convert it to a full refund, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

ERP. The 2.50 PIE (Kim Keat Link) gantry lies on the optimal route and is credited inside the recomputed fare. DRIVER COMPENSATION. None is due: the rider was billed 24.0 km against a 23.97 km trace, so there is no unbilled distance, and the POL-RD-04 compensation limb does not fire.

OUTCOME: PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 13.70 to the rider. The rider's claim is only partly made out — the measured excess is 5.97 km, not 6 km, and the refund is capped by the arithmetic — but the deviation is real and the fare had to be recomputed on the optimal route, which is what the 13.70 restores.
